items.label: Terrain is built from cube primitives (BoxGeometry or 8-corner cube faces), not only spheres/planes
items.evidence: const boxGeo = new THREE.BoxGeometry(VOXEL, VOXEL, VOXEL);
items.reason: The terrain is constructed using BoxGeometry primitives.

items.label: Cubes are placed in bulk over the island (cell loops, InstancedMesh of boxes, merged cube buffers)
items.evidence: const terrainMesh = new THREE.InstancedMesh(boxGeo, terrainMat, voxelData.length);
items.reason: The code uses InstancedMesh to render the terrain voxels in bulk.

items.label: Land sits on a discrete cell grid, not continuous vertex displacement of a plane
items.evidence: const wx = gx - HALF; const wz = gz - HALF;
items.reason: Terrain is generated based on integer grid coordinates gx and gz.

items.label: Columns and cliffs are stacks of unit cubes, not one stretched prism per cell
items.evidence: voxelData.push({ x: wx, y: h, z: wz, color: col });
items.reason: The code explicitly pushes multiple vertical layers (surface and sub-surface) for each grid cell.

items.label: The ground itself is cubes (a sun or UI may use planes)
items.evidence: const terrainMesh = new THREE.InstancedMesh(boxGeo, terrainMat, voxelData.length);
items.reason: The terrain is composed entirely of cube-based instanced meshes.

items.label: Land cubes snap to integer cell positions; no fractional offsets or random world-space cubes
items.reason: Voxels are positioned at integer coordinates derived from the grid loop.

items.label: One cell size for land/structure cubes, not scaled blobs
items.reason: All terrain cubes use a uniform size defined by the VOXEL constant.

items.label: An ocean or river is actually built
items.reason: The code generates terrain and waterfalls, but no actual ocean or water volume is built.

items.label: Every water body is supported: resting on blocks or walled by a solid rim, or visibly falling (waterfalls off edges). Static water is fine; this is about support, not simulation
items.reason: There is no water body built, only decorative waterfall meshes.

items.label: Still water sits on solid terrestrial blocks (sand/stone/dirt/bedrock) beneath it, not a flat sheet over the void
items.reason: No water body exists to have a bed.

items.label: Flora, fauna and structures are placed on the island's own cells, not thrown at random world coordinates
items.reason: Trees and fauna are placed at coordinates relative to the terrain height (h + 1).
